findings.reason: apply.js:52-63 now breaks after the first '\' line. For '-foo','\','+bar','\' only addEOFNL is set, and lines 70-72 push '' when the source has no trailing newline, so 'foo' becomes 'bar\n'. The diff deletes the old `if (addEOFNL)` branch inside `if (removeEOFNL)` that covered this case. C2 describes the same deleted branch and root cause, so it is merged here.
findings.claim: The new `break` stops the EOF-marker scan at the first '\ No newline' line, and the diff removes the branch for both markers being set. Patches whose old and new final lines both lack a trailing newline now get a newline added at EOF (or fail to apply), so createPatch output no longer round-trips.
findings.evidence: The loop at lines 52-63 now `break`s right after the first '\' line. For a final hunk `-foo` / `\ No newline` / `+bar` / `\ No newline`, the first marker follows a '-' line, so addEOFNL=true, the loop exits, and removeEOFNL stays false. Line 70 `else if (addEOFNL)` then runs `lines.push('')` when the source has no trailing newline. Source 'foo' therefore patches to 'bar\n' instead of 'bar'. Before the change both flags were set and the deleted `if (addEOFNL)` branch left EOF alone.

findings.evidence: diff.patch touches only src/patch/apply.js. In test/patch/apply.js, every hunk that uses '\ No newline at end of file' has exactly one marker (e.g. lines 121-151 and 1495-1553), so the case where both flags were set before the change is never exercised.
